data.note:
Reflection note:

Conclusion was incorrect. Unblinded specimen is mitoxantrone - PubChem CID 4212 (e16) and ChEMBL CHEMBL58 mechanisms are DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor and DNA inhibitor (e16), BBBC021 annotation DNA replication. Literature confirms this: Poirier 1986 review of mitoxantrone (PMID 3512224) and Evison et al. 2016 "Mitoxantrone, More than Just Another Topoisomerase II Poison" (PMID 26286294) describe mitoxantrone as a topoisomerase II poison/DNA intercalator.

Why Aurora was chosen: 0.1-1µM wells showed classic failed-cytokinesis morphology - cell_area z +13.1, cell_major_axis +14.9, cell_roundness -19.1, frac_multinucleate_proxy +15.3, frac_large_nucleus +12-61, nuc_solidity -29.8, nuc_form_factor -18.7 (e3,e4) with microscopist reporting large flat binucleate cells, enlarged irregular nuclei, intact tubulin/actin and high act_std/contrast (e7,e8). This overlaps strongly with Aurora B inhibition, and dose-response showed progressive rounding (rho +1.0 p=0,e11) with cytotoxicity at 10µM (6 cells, cell_roundness +39.4, tub_glcm_contrast +34.1 e2) which degraded signal.

What was missed: The per-well NSC correctly identified DNA replication for the 0.1µM well (similarity 0.663, e6) but the 4-well majority vote fell to Protein degradation 2/4 with low similarities 0.51-0.62 (e6) due to noisy high-dose well and inclusion of protein synthesis/microtubule neighbours in k=10 (e6). Topoisomerase II inhibition causes DNA replication stress, G2 checkpoint bypass, endoreduplication and polyploid/multinucleate cells that phenocopys Aurora without direct Aurora inhibition - we relied on image morphology alone without DNA-content or mitotic marker validation. Next experiment proposed would have resolved this: p-H3 Ser10 / Aurora B pT232 plus flow DNA content to distinguish true Aurora-driven cytokinesis failure from topoisomerase-induced polyploidy.

reflection.text:
Unblinded compound is mitoxantrone - PubChem CID 4212 / ChEMBL CHEMBL58 annotated as DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor and DNA inhibitor (e15/e16). Truth scored as DNA replication, we submitted Aurora kinase inhibitors p=0.68 (e14). The error is phenocopy, not random misclassification, and the trajectory shows why.

What we got right:
- We correctly captured a failed cytokinesis / polyploidy phenotype across the low-intermediate dose range. At 0.1uM (w_426d1ce61c, 45 cells) frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+15.3, cell_major_axis z=+14.9, cell_area z=+13.1 with cell_roundness z=-19.1 (e4). At 1uM (w_71aa1c3eef, 46 cells) frac_large_nucleus z=+61.1, nuc_solidity z=-29.8 (e3). At 0.3uM (w_da9f3d3374, 72 cells) frac_large_nucleus z=+15.0 (e5). Density lower vs DMSO with enlarged low-solidity cells and intact tubulin network was noted in both microscopist calls (e7/e8). This discriminated against microtubule destabilizers, Eg5 inhibitors, actin disruptors, Epithelial - which we down-weighted correctly to p <=0.08.
- High-dose cytotoxicity was captured: 10uM w_8a03ddeae8 had only 6 cells measured with extreme cell_roundness z=+39.4, tub_glcm_contrast z=+34.1, cell_eccentricity z=-32.2 (e2), and dose_response showed cell_roundness rho=+1.00 p=0 (e11). That pattern is consistent with DNA intercalator / topo II poison induced cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis at high concentration, but we had no discriminant marker to separate it from mitotic rounding.

What misled us and what we missed:
1. Microscopist anchoring. Both describe_phenotype calls returned "Aurora kinase inhibitors" as the only concrete candidate (e7 4 observations, e8 7 observations). In update_hypotheses we explicitly weighted this over the atlas: "Microscopist consistently identifies Aurora failed cytokinesis, while NSC split low-similarity votes contradict microtubule/protein classes" and set Aurora 0.68 vs DNA replication 0.05 (e13). Mitoxantrone as a topoisomerase II poison PMID 26286294 and more generally targeting DNA topoisomerase II in cancer PMID 42442624 can produce decatenation failure, polyploidy, large irregular nuclei and multinucleation that is morphologically indistinguishable from Aurora B failure in Cell Painting without a mitotic phospho-marker. Our search "topoisomerase inhibitor multinucleation polyploidy Aurora phenotype" returned 0 hits (e18), so we had no literature check running to counter the visual call.

2. We mis-read compare_to_reference_atlas (e6). NSC vote was Protein degradation 2/4; k-neighbours Protein synthesis 4/10, Microtubule destabilizers 2/10, Cholesterol-lowering 1/10. DNA replication did not appear in the top k-nearest, and we treated e6 as low-similarity split and contradictory to Aurora. In hypothesis_history DNA replication was assigned only e6 as supporting and e7/e8 as contradicting with p=0.05. In fact the lack of Aurora in e6 should have reduced Aurora confidence - we inverted the signal. Protein synthesis/degradation votes likely reflect reduced cell size / translation stress phenotypes that overlap with DNA replication stress at high dose, but our acquired wells lacked a direct S-phase readout.

3. Acquisition and dose_response choices were insufficient to discriminate. We acquired 4 wells covering 0.1, 0.3, 1, 10uM, all rep 1, leaving no DMSO quantitative well and exhausting budget (e1). Dose_response over 4 wells, 4 doses gave non-significant trends: frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-0.80 p=0.2 (e9), cell_area rho=-0.80 p=0.2 (e10), frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.20 p=0.8 (e12). The only significant trend was high-dose rounding (e11). With n=4 and the 10uM well having n=6 cells, extreme z-scores are high-variance and the inverted U (large multinucleated cells at 0.1-1uM -> small rounded cells at 10uM) looks like Aurora dose escalation but is equally expected for topoisomerase II inhibition: polyploidization at sub-lethal doses, then G2 arrest / cell loss at cytotoxic doses. We did not acquire EdU incorporation, gamma-H2AX, or DNA content (>4N) that would separate replication/decatenation failure from Aurora B kinase inhibition.

4. Probability calibration. Review critique approved 0.68 as "calibrated" because runner-up was Protein degradation 0.10. Unblinding shows this was overconfident given contradictory atlas data and p>0.2 dose trends. We should have kept DNA replication / DNA damage higher and noted phenocopy risk explicitly, with next experiment being DNA replication stress vs mitotic markers rather than only phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 / Aurora B pT232.

Mitoxantrone PMID 3512224, PMID 35306571 confirms the compound identity matches the annotated DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor mechanism; the Cell Painting signature here is a phenocopy-driven misassignment, not a measurement error.
what_was_right: Polyploidy/failed cytokinesis phenotype quantified: frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+15.3 at 0.1uM (e4), frac_large_nucleus z=+61.1 and nuc_solidity z=-29.8 at 1uM (e3), consistent across doses
Correct rejection of microtubule/actin classes: intact tubulin network noted (e7/e8 critique) and act vs tub features inconsistent with destabilizer/stabilizer
High-dose extreme rounding and cell loss captured: 6 cells at 10uM, cell_roundness z=+39.4 (e2), dose_response rho=+1.00 (e11)
what_was_wrong: Overweighted microscopist Aurora call (e7/e8) and set DNA replication to 0.05 (e13) despite mitoxantrone being a topoisomerase II poison PMID 26286294 PMID 42442624
Dismissed compare_to_reference_atlas e6 (Protein degradation/synthesis) as low-similarity instead of recognizing absence of Aurora support as evidence against Aurora
Relied on 4 single-replicate wells with non-significant dose_response p=0.2-0.8 (e9,e10,e12) and high-variance 10uM well (n=6) to support a monotonic Aurora model
No discriminant acquisition for replication stress: no DMSO quantitative well, no DNA content, EdU, or DNA damage readout to separate topo II decatenation failure polyploidy from Aurora inhibition

2. We mis-read compare_to_reference_atlas (e6). NSC vote was Protein degradation 2/4; k-neighbours Protein synthesis 4/10, Microtubule destabilizers 2/10, Cholesterol-lowering 1/10. DNA replication did not appear in the top k-nearest, and we treated e6 as low-similarity split and contradictory to Aurora. In hypothesis_history DNA replication was assigned only e6 as supporting and e7/e8 as contradicting with p=0.05. In fact the lack of Aurora in e6 should have reduced Aurora confidence - we inverted the signal. Protein synthesis/degradation votes likely reflect reduced cell size / translation stress phenotypes that overlap with DNA replication stress at high dose, but our acquired wells lacked a direct S-phase readout.

3. Acquisition and dose_response choices were insufficient to discriminate. We acquired 4 wells covering 0.1, 0.3, 1, 10uM, all rep 1, leaving no DMSO quantitative well and exhausting budget (e1). Dose_response over 4 wells, 4 doses gave non-significant trends: frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-0.80 p=0.2 (e9), cell_area rho=-0.80 p=0.2 (e10), frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.20 p=0.8 (e12). The only significant trend was high-dose rounding (e11). With n=4 and the 10uM well having n=6 cells, extreme z-scores are high-variance and the inverted U (large multinucleated cells at 0.1-1uM -> small rounded cells at 10uM) looks like Aurora dose escalation but is equally expected for topoisomerase II inhibition: polyploidization at sub-lethal doses, then G2 arrest / cell loss at cytotoxic doses. We did not acquire EdU incorporation, gamma-H2AX, or DNA content (>4N) that would separate replication/decatenation failure from Aurora B kinase inhibition.

4. Probability calibration. Review critique approved 0.68 as "calibrated" because runner-up was Protein degradation 0.10. Unblinding shows this was overconfident given contradictory atlas data and p>0.2 dose trends. We should have kept DNA replication / DNA damage higher and noted phenocopy risk explicitly, with next experiment being DNA replication stress vs mitotic markers rather than only phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 / Aurora B pT232.

Mitoxantrone PMID 3512224, PMID 35306571 confirms the compound identity matches the annotated DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor mechanism; the Cell Painting signature here is a phenocopy-driven misassignment, not a measurement error.

What was right:
- Polyploidy/failed cytokinesis phenotype quantified: frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+15.3 at 0.1uM (e4), frac_large_nucleus z=+61.1 and nuc_solidity z=-29.8 at 1uM (e3), consistent across doses
- Correct rejection of microtubule/actin classes: intact tubulin network noted (e7/e8 critique) and act vs tub features inconsistent with destabilizer/stabilizer
- High-dose extreme rounding and cell loss captured: 6 cells at 10uM, cell_roundness z=+39.4 (e2), dose_response rho=+1.00 (e11)

What was wrong or missed:
- Overweighted microscopist Aurora call (e7/e8) and set DNA replication to 0.05 (e13) despite mitoxantrone being a topoisomerase II poison PMID 26286294 PMID 42442624
- Dismissed compare_to_reference_atlas e6 (Protein degradation/synthesis) as low-similarity instead of recognizing absence of Aurora support as evidence against Aurora
- Relied on 4 single-replicate wells with non-significant dose_response p=0.2-0.8 (e9,e10,e12) and high-variance 10uM well (n=6) to support a monotonic Aurora model
- No discriminant acquisition for replication stress: no DMSO quantitative well, no DNA content, EdU, or DNA damage readout to separate topo II decatenation failure polyploidy from Aurora inhibition

Proposed next experiment: If reopened: 24h treatment at 0.1, 0.3, 1uM mitoxantrone vs DMSO and a reference topoisomerase II inhibitor, with EdU pulse, gamma-H2AX, and DNA content flow cytometry for >4N, plus parallel phospho-H3 Ser10; this directly tests DNA replication/decatenation failure vs Aurora B mitotic failure, which Cell Painting features alone (frac_large_nucleus, frac_multinucleate_proxy, nuc_solidity) cannot resolve here.
